item.description:
First launch shows one sheet, and a note ignored by git no longer opens unmarked after an agent writes to it.
- First launch offers to install agent hooks and no longer stacks the default-app sheet on Welcome; Settings > General still sets the default app. (#181) - Dewline offers to install agent hooks once for each folder holding `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.codex`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. In 0.4.0 the first offer was the only one, so a later agent folder was never offered. (#181) - Settings > Agents shows hooks as set up right after Set Up finishes. (#181) - Command-T in a window with no folder asks for one, like Command-N; Cancel opens no tab. (#181) - An agent write to a note that `.gitignore` ignores, such as `CLAUDE.local.md`, is marked again. This corrects 0.4.0, which skipped ignored notes. The scan lists tracked notes first, then ignored ones, newest first, within the 10,000-note cap. (#183) - A scan of closed notes also covers `.mdx` and `.qmd` files and the `.agents`, `.codex`, `.kiro`, `.ruler`, `.specify` and `.windsurf` folders. (#183) - Marks are kept on every landing of an outside change, including one that lands into unsaved typing or mid-conflict. (#183) - A save that waits more than 5 seconds on another app, such as a sync client, fails and retries, so quitting no longer hangs behind it. (#183) - README and the site state iCloud and iPhone behavior as designed: the device test in `docs/sync.md` has not been run. The README no longer quotes the 0.1.0 performance run. (#182)

Fewer settings and no Documents folder made for you, new notes go where you picked, and agent edits from Cursor and shell commands are named more accurately. Keeping an iCloud version no longer throws the other one away.
- Keep This Version on an iCloud conflict first saves the other version into the note's snapshots, so File > Earlier Versions can restore it. If that save fails, or the note keeps no snapshots, the other version stays unresolved with iCloud. (#178) - Closing a note in the middle of a conflict keeps the conflict as a marked change over the other version; Revert puts yours back. A Keep, or a change that lands over unsaved typing, also keeps its marks across close. This corrects the 0.3.0 note that conflict cards were not kept. (#178) - Settings drops Motion, Heading style, Smart Punctuation, Open notes in, When Dewline opens and New notes go in. Smart Punctuation stays in the Edit menu and the palette. (#173) - First launch no longer writes `~/Documents/Dewline`. Welcome opens in a window with no folder, and a note anywhere in `~/Library` opens without scanning it. (#173) - Command-N, New Folder and New Window with no folder window ask for a folder and remember it; Settings > General shows it as New notes go in once set, and Restore Defaults clears it. If the folder is gone, you are asked again, and Cancel makes nothing. Command-T in a window with no folder leaves the note untitled until you save it. (#173, #174, #177) - Export opens in the note's folder. Quick Open and Find in Files list gitignored notes while Show files .gitignore hides is on. (#173) - Renaming or moving a note no longer freezes the window while links to it are rewritten, and File > Rename can be undone. (#177) - Closing a note that another app deleted after a refused save shows the save sheet. (#177) - Git status: files whose only change is the executable bit are not listed when `core.fileMode` is off; CRLF files are not listed under `core.autocrlf`; Git LFS files compare against their pointer. SHA-256 repositories show no status. (#172) - A Cursor edit to a closed note is named Cursor instead of Another app. The shell-command mark applies only to notes under the folder the Bash command ran in. (#179) - Dewline offers to install agent hooks once at first launch and when you open a folder holding `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.codex`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. `dewline doctor` also reads that folder's project hook files and reports "hooks off" when `disableAllHooks` is set. (#179) - Pasting or dropping text into a CRLF note inserts CRLF. (#179) - A scan of closed notes skips what `.gitignore` ignores. Past 10,000 notes it keeps the most recently modified. (#178) - Release builds no longer run a performance check. (#170)

iCloud conflicts ask which version stays, files you open from Finder get the right folder, Revert works after you type around a change, and agent edits from shell commands and Cursor are marked.
- When iCloud keeps two versions of a note, a sheet names the other version's device and time and asks which stays. Use the Other Version lands as a marked change that Revert undoes. Saves now go through file coordination, so iCloud sees them. Welcome and the docs have a new Sync and mobile page. (#146, #165) - A file opened from Finder, `dewline open` or Open Recent opens in the window whose folder holds it, else on its git root, else on its parent folder. Command-N there writes in that window's folder. The open tabs are saved as you change them, so a crash reopens them. Many tabs on one folder share one watch and one scan. (#147) - A note in your home folder opens as a single-file window instead of scanning all of home and `~/Library`. Closing or quitting after another app deletes a note you have typed in shows the save sheet. Settings > General and a first-launch sheet offer to make Dewline the default app, and `.mdc`, `.mdx` and `.qmd` files open from File > Open and Open With. Code file types leave Open With. (#164) - A change from a Claude Code shell command is marked "During Claude Code's shell command" instead of Another app. Setup installs Cursor hooks, so Cursor's file edits carry its name; Settings shows Codex as Needs trust until you trust it. (#149) - Revert works after you type next to a change and keeps your typing. When you typed inside the change, the stamp says so. (#155) - The sidebar, Quick Open, Find in Files and [[ completion follow .gitignore the way git does: nested files, `.git/info/exclude`, your global ignore file, and negations. `[[` completion lists notes without freezing the window. (#153, #150, #166) - Git status shows a staged rename with edits as Renamed, and a rename into a subfolder as Renamed. (#150) - Exported HTML, PDF and the preview page color code blocks. (#150) - Source mode shows line numbers. The scroller rail ticks H1, H2 and H3. Wide Mermaid flowcharts fold into bands so labels stay readable, and inline code in a wrapped table column no longer breaks at a slash. (#151) - A new note takes its name from its first line when you leave it or close it, Command-T notes too, and an empty Untitled note you never typed in is removed when you close it. File > Share is the system share menu. (#156) - Return in a CRLF note inserts CRLF. Links to a note follow it when you rename it from File > Rename, drag it in the sidebar, or move or rename its folder. Replace All and link rewrites in closed notes show as yours, not Another app. (#166) - Only Markdown files list as changed while a note is closed; a hooked write to a `.env` or other file no longer does. Notes in `.claude`, `.cursor` and `.github` get closed-note changes, and `.mdc` files count as Markdown. Marks for undecided changes survive a crash. (#165) - Security fixes: a dangling symlink as the last part of a note path is refused, so a save cannot follow it to `~/.ssh`; moving a symlinked folder no longer rewrites the files it points to; and a Rust panic in any of twenty core calls shows an error or an empty result instead of crashing the app. (#157, #158, #168)

Notes save themselves, undecided changes survive closing, and export gains seven more formats; live collaboration, the agent chat panel, Follow Changes, the Preview pane and the font catalog are gone.
- Closing a tab, quitting, sleeping the Mac or switching apps saves your notes with no save sheet. Typing without a pause saves within 10 seconds. When a save is refused, the status bar says why and offers Save Now, and the text is kept as a draft that reopening the note offers to restore. Symlinked notes save in place. - Changes you have not decided on survive closing a tab and quitting, and reopening shows them at the same lines. A write to a closed note by another app, or while Dewline was quit, shows up as marked changes when you open it, and the sidebar badges the note with the writer and the count. Reading a note no longer credits an agent for someone else's later write. - A new look: the window, toolbar, tab strip and sidebar are redrawn, with a new palette, Seravek for text and SF Mono for code. The scroller rail shows headings and waiting changes, each change is reviewed at the change, and the sidebar shows each file's git status. - Tab and Shift-Tab move between table cells, and Tab in the last cell adds a row. Format > Insert Row and Insert Column edit a table. View > Zoom In, Zoom Out and Actual Size (Command-+, Command-- and Command-0) resize the text. Pasted JPEG, GIF, WebP and PNG images keep their original bytes. Edit > Copy as Markdown and Copy as HTML, and pasting from a web page or Mail gives Markdown. - Export to plain text, RTF, OpenDocument, EPUB, LaTeX, PNG and portable Markdown, besides PDF, Word and HTML. Portable Markdown turns wikilinks into relative links and copies images beside the file. - Code blocks highlight 50 languages, in Quick Look too. Hovering a block shows its language and a Copy button. Settings > Editor has Open code files, off by default: with it on, code files open in the editor as code, with the same highlighting, line numbers and no Markdown rendering. - Find in Files takes regular expressions, a `path:` filter and a Replace field. Replace All asks first, counts what it changed, and is one undo in an open note. - View > Sidebar Outline swaps the tree for the note's headings. Typing [[ lists the folder's notes. Renaming a note in the sidebar rewrites the links to it across the folder, and undo points them back. View > Backlinks lists the notes that link to the open note and opens each one at its link. - The `.claude`, `.cursor` and `.github` folders and `.mdc` files show in the tree, Quick Open and Find in Files. `dewline open <folder>` opens a folder in its window, and File > Open Recent lists recent folders and notes. - Settings has four panes: General, Editor, Appearance and Agents. There are four themes: Tidewater and Onionskin for light, Nightwatch and Carbon for dark, and a retired theme becomes the nearest of these. Body, headings and code take any font on your Mac. Link previews stay off until you turn them on in Settings > Editor. - File > Capture is the one place in the app that adds a line to your inbox. The Service, the App Intent, `dewline capture` and MCP work as before, and Settings > General holds the inbox path. - Agent setup skips agents you have not installed and says when Codex needs to trust Dewline's hooks. Edits made with curly quotes or in CRLF files are matched, so more agent edits carry the agent's name, and a failed edit no longer delays the next change. A nightly test runs Claude Code and Codex against these checks. - Removed: live collaboration is off for now, so Share, Join Shared Note and `dewline://join` are not in this build. The agent chat panel, Follow Changes, the Preview pane, the font catalog and installable fonts, the extra theme pack, and the daily note, Dock capture and capture shortcut are gone. - Security fixes in the URL scheme and in LaTeX and EPUB export.

A new look and a calmer window, a live preview, and a panel for your own coding agent.
- The window title names the open note and its folder. The sidebar starts at your folder's name, with + for a new note, and a native toolbar replaces the old top bar. - Open the preview to see the note rendered on the right while you edit its Markdown on the left. - Chat with your own coding agent beside the note. Dewline talks to it over the Agent Client Protocol, and its edits arrive marked, with Keep and Revert. Dewline ships no model and needs no account. - Links are quieter. A link on its own line shows a preview card, and hovering a link shows one; Settings turns previews off. - Which instruction files your agents read in a folder now shows in the status bar. - Reopening a note brings you back to the same place in it. - Sharing a note works again: the share popover opens, and join requests show in the status bar with Approve and Deny. - `dewline export --to pdf` writes the PDF again. - A new app icon, and headings use the system font by default.

The first public build. Dewline is a native Markdown editor for Mac: it opens the .md files you already keep, in place, and renders them as you write. Links, embeds, math, diagrams, export and live collaboration are built in, and every save changes only what you edited. No account and no telemetry.
- Open any Markdown file and edit it in place. Syntax hides until the caret reaches it; tables, task boxes, footnotes, callouts and highlighted code render in the page, and math and Mermaid diagrams are drawn natively. Wikilinks, embeds and #tags follow Obsidian's syntax. - Saves change only the bytes you edited, and never overwrite a newer version on disk. File > Snapshots restores an earlier version of the file. Export to HTML, PDF or DOCX, and preview .md files in Finder with Quick Look. - Open a folder or an Obsidian vault in place. A sidebar for the folder and your agent files, tabs, Quick Open (Shift-Command-O), find in files (Shift-Command-F) and one palette for files, commands and settings (Shift-Command-P). - Edit a file live with someone by invite link, peer to peer. - Six themes plus a pack of four, installable fonts, Vim mode, a Source view, and focus and typewriter modes. - When git, a sync app, a script or a coding agent changes the open file, Dewline marks each change, and names the agent when its hooks report it. Keep or revert each one, or all at once; Dewline snapshots the file first. - `dewline open file.md:12 --wait` works as `$EDITOR`, `dewline notify` lets agent hooks name their edits, and `dewline mcp` serves a folder's notes to an agent.
